ENG-2442 already revoked EXECUTE from PUBLIC, so that is background, not work. **Also 2026-11-14, agreed:** the first iteration ships without per-session sign-out (second iteration, task group 8), but needs the hosted Supabase Auth setting "require current password". Without it a read-only session can set a new password, sign in, and get an unregistered full-access session. MCP spec blocks p6To3ZtUI, fkb-jVcxG, XOl2KjKyt were edited directly to match (the user prefers direct edits over notes when adjusting to decisions). Say "the Supabase setting" when naming it: the user first read "require current password" as a feature to build.

The OpenSpec change `agent-read-only-access` (read-only Supabase access for AI agents) finished planning on 2026-09-16. All four artifacts are in `openspec/changes/agent-read-only-access/` and pass `openspec validate --strict`. **Implementation has not started.** The user starts it with `/opsx:apply`.

**Where it lives.** The user pasted the artifacts into Roam as [OpenSpec/Agent read-only access](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/DHOqLFwkT). Top-level block UIDs: Spec `OHfAX-ANr`, Proposal `wo1G9LSI9`, Design `xzNpL58c4`, Tasks `h_Lgn1Ro0`. The broader context (identity, read-only tokens, writing agents) is in block [-Q3X_phzD](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/-Q3X_phzD), a TODO for Joel Chan. Direct Roam writes work since 2026-10-23 (see [[roam-propose-write-quirks]]); keep the local files and the page in step by hand. The user doesn't plan to commit the local files; Roam is the home.

**2026-10-31 changes (in both copies):**
- "Alternative to consider: a restricted session of the principal, without an agent user" section after Migration Plan (Roam Eg4aD33rW). The hook gives one registered session of the principal `agent_reader`. Explicitly **not a decision**; still being weighed against decision 1. Trade: immediate revocation and separate identity vs fewer moving parts.
- New risk: Edge Functions write with the service key, so the role doesn't stop them (Roam YF7DRHmiF). Mitigation is a shared caller check. **No task added**: the tasks describe the original design while the choice is open.
- The grant requirement now reads "a logged-in (non-agent) user" (the user's edit).
- Trang Doan's question (VgqKSYHkc) was answered by the user: agents are identified by `role`, and more generally by joining `agent_grant.agent_id`. The column name isn't fixed in the design yet.

**Decisions the user settled, and that should not be reopened:**
- **Agent identity.** Each grant creates its own auth user with `auth.users.role = 'agent_reader'`, set through `auth.admin.createUser({ role })`. Supabase Auth reapplies that role to every token it issues. Self-signed JWTs were rejected: asymmetric keys, and a password-reset escalation when `sub` is the principal.
- **Delegation.** An `agent_grant` row maps the agent to its principal, and `my_user_accounts()` adds the principal and the principal's groups. No access rows are copied, and the 18 direct `auth.uid()` checks stay as they are. The user first worried this copied rows into `group_membership`. It does not, because the function only reads the principal's memberships.
- **Enforcement.** Grants enforce read-only, not RLS.
- **Function execution.** `EXECUTE` is revoked from `PUBLIC` globally. The user first wanted this per function, then agreed global is safer. Every function already has explicit `anon`, `authenticated`, and `service_role` grants, checked in `pg_proc`, so anonymous reads (ENG-1837) and `create-space` are unaffected.
- **Where grant management runs.** A Supabase Edge Function `create-agent` (like `create-group`), plus RPC and RLS for listing and revoking. There is no Vercel endpoint. The UI is on the website under `auth/`, not in the plugins.
- **What the grant holds.** No expiry and no permission column. Writing agents (future) get `role: authenticated`, and the access they inherit is capped with `SpaceAccessPermissions`. Finer operation kinds become extra Postgres roles.
- **Agent email domain.** `agents.discoursegraphs.com`.

{"uid":"8wg9mn-Kt","markdown":"- Glossary <roam uid="8wg9mn-Kt"/>
  - **Space**: one Roam graph or Obsidian vault connected to Discourse Graphs. <roam uid="V3WnEIow4"/>
  - **Pseudo-user**: a login (a row in `auth.users`) that stands for something other than a person: a space, a group, or `everyone`. <roam uid="pvL47ThL3"/>
  - **Space password, space session**: the shared credential stored in the platform settings. Every member of the graph can read it. Logging in with it means acting as the space, not as a person. <roam uid="aCzLIN3E9"/>
  - **Personal account, personal session**: a Discourse Graphs account for one person, and a login as that person. Neither exists yet. <roam uid="gav2kohTZ" refs="1"/>
  - **Platform account** (`PlatformAccount`): a person as a platform knows them. A Roam user has the same uid, so the same platform account, in every graph. An Obsidian platform account belongs to one vault. <roam uid="QH3QWTy6q"/>
  - **`LocalAccess`**: the record that a platform account takes part in a space. <roam uid="u7kJsZCjS"/>
  - **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space. <roam uid="PrKq7VlbT"/>
  - **Claim**: a personal account's statement "this platform account is me". It is stored on the platform account (`dg_account`). <roam uid="_ditzi8bq"/>
  - **Vouching space**: the space whose session made the claim. Because that session is shared, it shows only that someone in that space made the claim, not who. <roam uid="w9yVmbPyd"/>
  - **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven. <roam uid="0ifLRtPpZ" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - **Access claim, identity claim**: an access claim only lets the person act in the vouching space. An identity claim says who the person is everywhere, and so carries attribution. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record. <roam uid="xwIIr5Cdw"/>
  - **Reach**: the spaces a person can act for through their claims. <roam uid="_blIoPRFG"/>
  - **Lease**: a person's access through a space lasts while they keep using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). 90 days is a placeholder. <roam uid="gegO9HCwc"/>
  - **Cap**: a limit on what a claim or a grant allows, for example read-only. <roam uid="gIBK30HQq"/>
  - **Group**: a set of spaces that share content with each other. Each group has a pseudo-user. <roam uid="cqn2EyIWs"/>
  - **`everyone`**: the pseudo-user that public content is shared with. Every caller counts as `everyone`, logged in or not. <roam uid="u2sj1P4VN"/>
  - **Agent**: an AI agent that logs in with a restricted session of its principal (a person or a space), usually read-only. It is not a separate user: it reads what its principal reads. <roam uid="Z4tFuDPOk"/>
","path":["Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="18"/>"],"queriedAt":"2026-11-14T22:44:42.486Z","graph":"discourse-graphs"}

{"uid":"Czog3Tth-","markdown":"- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>

{"uid":"1Jt5g8iXN","markdown":"- Constraints so far <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h"/>
    - Note from Michael: Actually we should look into the pros and cons of that assumption. Forcing accounts is harder on user, but there are engagement benefits. <roam uid="2YMqhsRfX"/>
  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone can join a uid that has no members yet) is closed before any of this work. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>

  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew"/>

{"uid":"0m3bnPqzF","markdown":"- UX touchpoints: where a person must see how they are logged in <roam uid="0m3bnPqzF"/>
  - **Why it matters:** a plugin holds a space session and maybe a personal session, and a personal claim can be asserted, attested, frozen or expired. The same action gives different results in each state, often silently: RLS returns an empty list, not an error. Every surface below has to tell the person which state applies, or they will read "no access" as "nothing there". Each touchpoint is UI work, so this list is also a cost. <roam uid="Xt_tFK4O3"/>
  - States the UI has to distinguish <roam uid="yLQbi5f0O" hiddenChildren="8"/>
  - Plugins (Roam and Obsidian) <roam uid="OAX4TOvkq" hiddenChildren="13"/>
  - Website <roam uid="iIll2saun" hiddenChildren="5"/>
  - Outside the apps <roam uid="75G9IK3Ox" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Edge cases that change what a touchpoint shows <roam uid="d5N1Dq8K8" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Open: which touchpoints the first release needs. Cross-space search, the status indicator and connect/reconnect look like the most likely first targets, because search is the first feature that depends on the personal session. <roam uid="ibhjghgwf"/>
","path":["Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="18"/>"],"queriedAt":"2026-11-14T22:44:44.404Z","graph":"discourse-graphs"}

{"uid":"8okk-_Uer","markdown":"- Facts to verify before relying on them <roam uid="8okk-_Uer"/>
  - Answered: a Roam client can't set `:create/user` on its own writes. `roamAlphaAPI.data.block.create` ignores an attempt to set it to another user and records the caller, and the older `roamDatomicAlphaAPI` isn't present (tested from the console, 2026-10-24). A block's creator is therefore trustworthy evidence of which Roam user wrote it. <roam uid="I_T0KWw31" refs="1"/>
  - Does the Roam backend API return `:user/email` for users of the graph? Cautious assumption: no, since Roam shows each user only their own email. L6 would then prove who supplies the token, but couldn't attest other members. <roam uid="pncmfqVMJ"/>
  - Does a Roam import keep the original `:create/user` and `:create/time`? <roam uid="ihRxT-Vwx"/>
  - ORCID: mostly answered. ORCID's own OAuth sign-in returns an authenticated ORCID iD, so the Website can verify an ORCID for attribution as its own OAuth client. Supabase also accepts custom OAuth and OIDC providers (identifier `custom:...`, up to 3 on the free plan, unlimited on Pro), so ORCID can be a login provider as well. Still open: whether linking a custom-provider identity to an existing account works (the docs don't say), and ORCID usually doesn't release an email, so the provider needs `email_optional`. <roam uid="4nPdcx1yb"/>
  - Answered: an Obsidian `PlatformAccount` is created by the plugin, with an id made of the vault name and a random suffix, stored in the plugin settings. It is local to one vault, but a vault synced between devices or people shares the same id. <roam uid="pcJRRqX-t"/>
  - Can the Supabase OAuth 2.1 Server flow complete inside the plugins? Roam has no protocol handler, so it would need a popup that hands the result back to the page. Obsidian can register an `obsidian://` handler. <roam uid="llUBOTvj7"/>
  - ATProto: its OAuth profile requires DPoP and pushed authorization requests, which a Supabase custom provider probably doesn't support (expected, not tested). Assume ATProto login or identity verification needs its own flow on the Website. The verified handle or `did:plc` would then be stored as a trusted identifier, like ORCID. <roam uid="E0XuKzFaB"/>
  - Assumed, not checked: the Obsidian plugin can't read the email of the signed-in Obsidian account. The plugin API (`obsidian` 1.8.7) exposes no account or email, and Obsidian is protective of user privacy, so we design as if it never can. If that changes, Obsidian accounts could be proven by email like Roam accounts. <roam uid="SnaEEHkZI"/>
","path":["Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="18"/>"],"queriedAt":"2026-11-14T22:44:44.726Z","graph":"discourse-graphs"}

  - ATProto: its OAuth profile requires DPoP and pushed authorization requests, which a Supabase custom provider probably doesn't support (expected, not tested). Assume ATProto login or identity verification needs its own flow on the Website. The verified handle or `did:plc` would then be stored as a trusted identifier, like ORCID. <roam uid="E0XuKzFaB"/>
  - Assumed, not checked: the Obsidian plugin can't read the email of the signed-in Obsidian account. The plugin API (`obsidian` 1.8.7) exposes no account or email, and Obsidian is protective of user privacy, so we design as if it never can. If that changes, Obsidian accounts could be proven by email like Roam accounts. <roam uid="SnaEEHkZI"/>

Goal: turn the page into the project design document. It holds the vision, the threat model, the staging ladder, and the decisions that span stages. Each stage becomes its own OpenSpec change when it is scheduled.

Method:
- Move whole sections with `move_block`, so UIDs and references keep working. Rewrite only blocks that are stale.
- Write new blocks only for the note, the threat model's introduction and the decisions index.
- Do it one section at a time, re-reading each section before changing it, and checking it after.

Status words used throughout: **Settled**, **Leaning**, **Open**, **Deferred** (with what it waits for).

## New order

### 1. Note (S4dKzvDG9), rewritten
- What the page is: the project design document for personal accounts. It covers the vision, the threat model, the stages, and the decisions that span stages.

- Replaces "only the items under Constraints are settled" and the "pre-spec" line.

### 2. Why personal accounts
- Goal (Czog3Tth-), unchanged: the end state.
- What personal accounts unblock (xf04Pfzph), unchanged. The "below this line, for later" separator (IP1CB4pWB) has nothing under it; remove it.

### 3. Glossary (8wg9mn-Kt)
Kept here, after the why, because the threat model and the model use its terms. Updates:
- Lease: the leaning is now unlimited, so drop "90 days is a placeholder".
- Co-member: keep the term, and add "space password holder", the wider attacker the threat model uses.
- Access claim and identity claim become weak and strong claims, the staging vocabulary. Attestation level stays, as the stored form of that difference.
- Personal account: drop "Neither exists yet" once v0 ships. Not now.

### 4. Where we are today
- Current state (wV0qa8Lj7). Stale lines:
  - `everyone` is "ENG-1837 branch, not merged": check before editing.

### 5. Threat model (new parent)
- Who the attacker is: any holder of any space's password who knows the victim's account id, not only a co-member. Taken from the attack scripts. Includes the shared-row fact, with a link to candidate P8VX99a0V.
- The existing threat block (6q9kdzcJl), moved here from the identity-link decision and widened to match.
- Why attacker skill is no barrier: a short version of `dg-accounts-attacker-skill.md`.
- Attack scripts (97tr4Tlhm), moved here from "WIP on attack vectors". The WIP parent (pLowWcWrj) then goes away.
- Rule for shared values: platform account values are shared on purpose. Hardening tightens who may write them; we never keep copies per space.

### 6. The model: how accounts work at every stage
Generic material, true at every stage, gathered from three sections:
- Claims through a platform account: the model (j2yrxCKys), the ruled-out options (1FYnwOB2T) and its properties (6mRqlz_K_), all from "how a person gets a space's access".
  - Its lease line should say "unlimited (leaning)".

- Sessions: two sessions (A8N_Jsvr1) and delivery through Supabase's OAuth server (anOlv9O2J), moved from "Personal session in the plugins", whose status becomes settled. Social login: the plugin hands off to the Website.

### 7. Staging: accounts v0 and the steps after it (JR6Iua-UN)

- **v0, not covered yet:** search consent. It should state the cost of "read access is enough" plainly: a member can bring a private graph's content into another graph, and that graph has no say.

### 8. Decisions index (new)

  - v0 narrow reach
  - claims only through a platform account
  - no edge from a person to a space
  - agents as sessions
  - delivery through Supabase's OAuth server
  - social login through the Website
  - shared platform account values

  - names shown, emails hidden

  - session storage in Roam: after the MCP token handoff and agent read-only access
  - old Roam emails we hold: after v0
  - `my_accounts` scope: after v0
- **Open after v0:**
  - proof layers and packages
  - space admin
  - profile visibility model
  - the email match in Roam
  - repairing agreement between spaces

### 9. Decision details (new parent; the long sections move here unchanged)
- How a personal account is linked to a platform identity (HrW3SuczV). Its threat block has moved to 5. It keeps two kinds of claim, verified identifiers, email as the bridge, layers, packages, and applies to every option. Two corrections:
  - Its L2 claim needs fixing (attack 3).
  - Its first paragraph should point to the threat model.
- How far a claim reaches (5XbPKQsOm, with its two options), moved out of "how a person gets a space's access", whose other parts went to 6. The heading becomes "Settled for v0: narrow. Later: by proof", with the options kept for the later steps.
- Whether to hide user ids (s86_P-XTI), unchanged.
- From "Other open decisions" (W8f_RJZgt), each child becomes its own entry here, and the parent goes away:
  - Space admin (3l40D2TI3)
  - Personal session storage (jQDFzycLX), marked deferred
  - Consent for cross-space search (fi-J8nr1F), marked settled
  - Personal information before consent (sPWWnb1Zg)
  - Profile visibility (S4MegNHAq)
  - Which accounts a caller can see (aY4D_LNku), marked deferred

### 10. UX touchpoints (0m3bnPqzF)
- Moved after the decisions. It depends on them.
- State names: "asserted, attested, frozen or expired" become weak, strong, held, and drop "expired" if leases are unlimited.
- "Open: which touchpoints the first release needs" is mostly answered by the v0 proposal. Link to it.
- The two wireframes stay in staging. This section links to them.

### 11. Facts to verify (8okk-_Uer)
- Split it into Open and Answered, with the open ones first.
- Add as answered: social login isn't done inside the plugin.

### 12. Appendix: diagrams
- The access-resolution image (0mR6YMCry) and the canvas (fHh1eG1Sn) move here, unless you want them inline.
- The canvas may still show agents as principals. Check it.
- The redrawn identities SVG (`dg-accounts-identities.svg`) still needs uploading. It probably replaces 0mR6YMCry.

## Questions before starting
1. Vocabulary: weak and strong claims everywhere, with attestation level as the stored form? Or keep the access and identity claim terms as well?
2. The attack scripts: a child of the threat model, or their own page linked from it? They will grow into slides.
3. Leases: does "unlimited" mean we drop the lease from the model, keeping revocation only by deleting the claim or the `LocalAccess` row? Or keep the `last_seen` column for later?

- **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven. <roam uid="0ifLRtPpZ"/>
  - `asserted`: only vouched for by a space session. Any co-member could have made it. <roam uid="tyAhKq0Iy"/>
  - `corroborated`: two or more spaces recorded the same platform account details before the claim (layer L2). <roam uid="F5NMd6BX2"/>
  - `attested`: proven by a check that a co-member can't fake, such as email binding (L1), a Roam backend token (L6) or a Roam sign-in token (L8). <roam uid="LT9VSLIoK"/>
  - `frozen`: a competing claim arrived, and the claim gives no access until it is settled (L3). <roam uid="jssPobCiC"/>

input.string: `attested`: proven by a check that a space password holder can't fake, such as a Roam backend token (L6) or a Roam sign-in token (L8). Email binding (L1) counts only once the email record itself can't be written under a space login (see the threat model, attack 2).

input.string: `frozen`: a competing claim arrived, and the claim gives no access until it is settled (L3). Whether v0 holds conflicting claims is still open.

input.string: **Weak claim, strong claim**: a weak claim's only evidence is the space session that made it, so any holder of that space's password could have made it; in v0 it reaches only that space. A strong claim carries a proof a password holder can't fake, and can reach all the platform account's spaces and carry attribution. Older sections call these an access claim and an identity claim. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record.

The difference is the attestation level, not a different record.

input.string: **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space. **Space password holder**: anyone who holds the password of some space, any space. The threat model uses this wider term, because many attacks don't need the attacker to share a space with the victim.

input.string: **Lease**: a limit on how long a person's access through a space lasts after they stop using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). Leaning: unlimited, so no expiry in v0.

content.text: Now the threat model, a new section at the end of the page for now. I'll put all the sections in order at the end.

input.markdown:
- Threat model
  - **Why it matters:** every stage below is judged by what it lets an attacker do. This section says who the attacker is and what they can reach. The attack scripts walk through each attack step by step, with the limits we ship and the steps that close each gap.
  - Who the attacker is: anyone who holds the password of some space, any space, and knows the victim's platform account id. A co-member is one case, not the only one.
    - Every member of a Roam graph can read its space password: the plugin keeps it in the props of its settings page (`getOrCreateSpacePassword`, `apps/roam/src/utils/supabaseContext.ts`). Anyone can also create a new space: the Website's space route checks only a name, a URL, a platform and a password.
    - A co-member sees the victim's Roam uid in the graph, since the plugin reads every member's uid to fill in `PlatformAccount`. A member of a space that shares a group with one of the victim's spaces can read it from `PlatformAccount` or `my_accounts`.
    - A Roam user is one `PlatformAccount` row, shared by every space they appear in. An editor of any space can list that account in their own space and write to the shared row. Our database can't check who belongs to a Roam graph, so a listing carries only the word of the space that wrote it. Issue candidate: ((P8VX99a0V)).
  - Attacker skill is no barrier
    - The plugins and the database schema are open source, so each function's name, parameters and access check can be read on GitHub.
    - An LLM writes the hand-made request from that code in minutes, and explains how to run it in the browser console.
    - A script written once can be reused by anyone.
    - The attackers are insiders with ordinary motives: credit for work, a falling-out, a departing student.
    - So we treat every space password holder as able to send any request our API accepts, and judge each stage by what it prevents against that person.
  - Shared values: platform account values (name, identifiers) are shared on purpose, because Roam shares them across graphs. We harden them by tightening who may write them (accept and audit, then self-reported, then proven), never by keeping a copy per space.

input.markdown:
- The model: how accounts work at every stage
  - **Why it matters:** this is what stays true from v0 on. The stages change how strong a claim can be and how far it reaches, not this model.
  - Sessions
    - Social login: the plugin doesn't offer it. It hands off to the Website, where the person logs in or creates an account by any method, social logins included.
  - Agents: an agent uses a restricted session of its principal, a space or a person, usually read-only. It is not a separate user and adds nothing to access resolution. See the agent read-only access OpenSpec change.

{"uid":"v-wdJK626","markdown":"- Personal session in the plugins <roam uid="v-wdJK626"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this sets how a person logs in from a plugin, and where the plugin keeps that login. In Roam, keeping the login across reloads exposes it to every other extension, and not keeping it costs a click after each reload. It also decides which work runs as the person and which as the space, because some functions break if the person replaces the space. <roam uid="XtAl_AlUO"/>
  - Delivery: leaning towards Supabase Auth acting as an OAuth server, with the plugin as an OAuth client (PKCE). The person logs in on the Website by whatever method their account uses, so password accounts work too. Fallback: a device-style flow over `secret_token`, where the plugin opens the Website and then polls for the session. <roam uid="anOlv9O2J"/>
    - The Supabase OAuth 2.1 Server has no separate charge. People who sign in through it count toward the project's monthly active users, like any other sign-in. Source: Supabase docs, OAuth 2.1 Server guide. Accepted as an added cost. <roam uid="Z6B0tGor7"/>
    - Completing the flow inside the plugin is nice to have, not required. If it can't, the flow completes in a browser tab: the Website receives the result and the plugin collects it through the `secret_token` fallback. <roam uid="HmGIe3SsJ"/>
    - Social login (Supabase `signInWithOAuth` and identity linking) is a separate need on the Website: adding external identities to an account, and logging in with them. <roam uid="THBV37Ayp"/>
    - A person may create their account with an external identity and keep logging in with it, without ever setting a password. The plugin flow works the same for them, because the login step happens on the Website. <roam uid="IrbMTsSJY"/>
    - External identities linked this way are verified by their provider, so they can also serve as trusted identifiers for attribution. ORCID is not a built-in provider (ENG-405). <roam uid="MtQhgD_oh"/>
  - Storage: never in graph settings or the vault's `data.json`, which other people can read or sync. In Roam, `localStorage` is shared with every extension. <roam uid="jQDFzycLX"/>
    - Supabase sets token lifetimes: the access token expires after the project's JWT expiry (one hour by default), and the refresh token lasts until it is used, revoked, or cut off by a session time-box or inactivity timeout, if the project sets one. <roam uid="sggTyBNKs"/>
    - These settings apply to the whole project, including Website sessions, not only to the plugins. <roam uid="qppZbZExq"/>
    - What the plugin decides is whether it keeps the refresh token: <roam uid="VNhkLUpxm" hiddenChildren="2"/>
    - Re-running the flow is cheap: the Website keeps its own login cookie on its own origin, which Roam extensions can't read. If the person is still logged in on the Website, the flow completes without typing anything. <roam uid="Rnxg83ODf"/>
    - Roam never reads the Website's cookie. The plugin opens a popup on the Website, the popup uses the cookie to skip the login form, and the Website sends an authorization code back to the plugin's page. The plugin exchanges the code for its own tokens, separate from the Website's session. <roam uid="D7aP7KN83"/>
    - A popup needs a user click, so after a reload the person clicks once to reconnect. A hidden iframe could avoid the click, but browsers increasingly block the cookies it would need. <roam uid="z-uzA5aW1"/>
    - Memory-only storage stops theft of tokens at rest. It doesn't stop a malicious extension that is running in the same page while the session is active, for example by wrapping `fetch`. <roam uid="OAS1AAkJ6"/>
    - Pending: keep tokens in memory in Roam (one click to reconnect after each reload), or keep the refresh token in `localStorage` (no click, but other extensions can steal it). Obsidian can store tokens on disk outside the vault either way. <roam uid="5YETQsAFC"/>
  - Two sessions: the plugin keeps the space session and adds a personal session when one is available. <roam uid="A8N_Jsvr1"/>
    - Downsides of switching the plugin from the space session to the personal session when one is available <roam uid="esLlHtygy" hiddenChildren="6"/>
    - Split: the personal session for reads, search and actions done as the person; the space session for sync, group membership and sharing. <roam uid="OhtCf8HO2"/>
","path":["Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="18"/>","Other open decisions (not yet mapped in detail) <roam uid="W8f_RJZgt"/>"],"queriedAt":"2026-11-14T22:56:37.862Z","graph":"discourse-graphs"}

{"uid":"6mRqlz_K_","markdown":"- Properties of the model <roam uid="6mRqlz_K_"/>
  - Lease: a last-seen time on `LocalAccess`. The plugin's space session already writes `LocalAccess` when the person is active, so renewing needs no personal session. <roam uid="ifJ1jpWX7"/>
  - Revocation: delete the `LocalAccess` row, let the lease expire, or remove the claim. <roam uid="b30OPBdFw"/>
  - Caps, for example read-only access through a space: a cap column on the claim. Permission functions must apply it, because `my_user_accounts()` returns bare ids. <roam uid="T1dfPIW2r"/>
  - Space admin: the group admin flag doesn't apply. The leaning is an admin flag and its strength on `LocalAccess`; see "Space admin" under the other open decisions. <roam uid="gKWGQT9Pb"/>
  - Visibility: claims stay private to the person. Space readers already see the space's `PlatformAccount` rows through `LocalAccess`. <roam uid="LzUYZ2I5u"/>
  - Sharing a space with a group: the rule "`SpaceAccess(G, S)` exists only while S's pseudo-user is a member of G" is checked on S, so an insert check enforces it unchanged. A person shares on behalf of the space. <roam uid="3zLQCYhH4"/>
  - Agents: an agent uses a restricted session of its principal, so it reaches what the principal reaches. It adds nothing to access resolution. The restriction, for example read-only, comes from the session. <roam uid="nc_m8SiQY"/>

{"uid":"vdV1jigrm","markdown":"- Open: keeping the claim (`dg_account`) out of ordinary account writes <roam uid="vdV1jigrm" refs="3"/>
  - **Why it matters:** editors must keep writing the platform accounts of their space's authors, but claiming is a separate operation with its own rules. Today any editor of a space can claim its unowned accounts (((vtxvgZEKp))). Not decided; postponed. <roam uid="e3dHDdJ0k"/>
  - Option 1, column privileges: revoke `INSERT` and `UPDATE` on `PlatformAccount` from `authenticated`, then grant them back on every column except `dg_account`. A table-level grant covers all columns, so revoking the one column alone does not work. Cost: each new column has to be added to the grants, and a client upsert that sends `dg_account`, even as null, fails. <roam uid="XbS0B2zbY"/>
  - Option 2, a separate table for the claim: the link between a person and a platform account moves out of `PlatformAccount`, and only the claim path writes it. This departs from "Where the claim lives, without a new table" above. <roam uid="eXQzoqBsj"/>
  - Both options route claims through a `SECURITY DEFINER` claim function that holds the claim rules in one place. If the claim moves later, only the function body changes. Today no client code sets `dg_account`: only space creation sets it, for the space's own account. ENG-2447 removed the Website's `POST /api/supabase/platform-account` route, which could set it but had no callers. <roam uid="ftEJrOez4"/>
  - Since ENG-2447 (October 30), `authenticated` can no longer write `dg_account` (column privileges, see ((vtxvgZEKp))<ref>Restrict claiming an unowned account to a logged-in person claiming a person account</ref>). Whatever claim mechanism this spec picks starts from there. <roam uid="JfuWa2pWN"/>

input.markdown: - Search consent: in v0, a person's read access to a space is enough to search it from another space, and spaces set no policy of their own. The cost: a member of a private graph can find its content while working in another graph and import it there, and the private graph has no say. They could already copy it by hand; search makes it routine.

input.string: Open: what happens when a second person claims an account that is already claimed. If the first claim wins, a forger can block the real owner, and from any space, since the claim sits on the shared `PlatformAccount` row. If the newest claim wins, two people can take the account back and forth.

input.string: Buys security: as specified, none. One person can control two spaces, or create them, and record the same details in both (threat model, attack 3). It would need a way to count only spaces the forger doesn't control.

toolu_01Scrcc3oQRFK69amottn78P.string: Buys security: as specified, none. One person can control two spaces, or create them, and record the same details in both (threat model, attack 3). It would need a way to count only spaces the forger doesn't control.

input.string: Buys security: stops a casual forger, but not one who sends a hand-made request, from any space where they hold the password. The email record comes from a plugin under a space login, so they can write their own email on the victim's account (threat model, attack 2). For Roam, the email match shouldn't widen reach until the record comes from a source a password holder can't write: device-signed reports, or Roam's server.

input.string: **Why it matters:** a plugin holds a space session and maybe a personal session, and a claim can be weak, strong, or held by a conflict. The same action gives different results in each state, often silently: RLS returns an empty list, not an error. Every surface below has to tell the person which state applies, or they will read "no access" as "nothing there". Each touchpoint is UI work, so this list is also a cost.

{"uid":"H3a0tja8D","markdown":"# Spec: DiscourseGraph Accounts <roam uid="H3a0tja8D" refs="18"/>

- [[>]] [[!NOTE]] Project design document: the vision, threat model, stages and decisions for personal accounts <roam uid="S4dKzvDG9"/>
  - This page describes where personal accounts are heading, what can go wrong, the stages we plan to ship, and the decisions that span those stages. Each decision is marked Settled, Leaning, Open or Deferred; the "Decisions index" lists them all. Part of [[Project/Discourse Graph Accounts]]. <roam uid="WOKj5fQ9w"/>
  - How it relates to OpenSpec: accounts v0 becomes one OpenSpec change once its decisions settle, and each later step becomes its own change when it is scheduled. A change's design records a decision in full; this page then marks the decision settled, with a link to the change. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agents acting for a person: an agent session of a person reads what that person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
- Glossary <roam uid="8wg9mn-Kt"/>
  - **Space**: one Roam graph or Obsidian vault connected to Discourse Graphs. <roam uid="V3WnEIow4"/>
  - **Pseudo-user**: a login (a row in `auth.users`) that stands for something other than a person: a space, a group, or `everyone`. <roam uid="pvL47ThL3"/>
  - **Space password, space session**: the shared credential stored in the platform settings. Every member of the graph can read it. Logging in with it means acting as the space, not as a person. <roam uid="aCzLIN3E9"/>
  - **Personal account, personal session**: a Discourse Graphs account for one person, and a login as that person. Neither exists yet. <roam uid="gav2kohTZ" refs="1"/>
  - **Platform account** (`PlatformAccount`): a person as a platform knows them. A Roam user has the same uid, so the same platform account, in every graph. An Obsidian platform account belongs to one vault. <roam uid="QH3QWTy6q"/>
  - **`LocalAccess`**: the record that a platform account takes part in a space. <roam uid="u7kJsZCjS"/>
  - **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space. **Space password holder**: anyone who holds the password of some space, any space. The threat model uses this wider term, because many attacks don't need the attacker to share a space with the victim. <roam uid="PrKq7VlbT"/>
  - **Claim**: a personal account's statement "this platform account is me". It is stored on the platform account (`dg_account`). <roam uid="_ditzi8bq"/>
  - **Vouching space**: the space whose session made the claim. Because that session is shared, it shows only that someone in that space made the claim, not who. <roam uid="w9yVmbPyd"/>
  - **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven, as stored on the claim. `asserted` is a weak claim; the other levels are kinds of strong claim, or a held one. <roam uid="0ifLRtPpZ" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - **Weak claim, strong claim**: a weak claim's only evidence is the space session that made it, so any holder of that space's password could have made it; in v0 it reaches only that space. A strong claim carries a proof a password holder can't fake, and can reach all the platform account's spaces and carry attribution. Older sections call these an access claim and an identity claim. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record. <roam uid="xwIIr5Cdw"/>
  - **Reach**: the spaces a person can act for through their claims. <roam uid="_blIoPRFG"/>
  - **Lease**: a limit on how long a person's access through a space lasts after they stop using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). Leaning: unlimited, so no expiry in v0. <roam uid="gegO9HCwc"/>
  - **Cap**: a limit on what a claim or a grant allows, for example read-only. <roam uid="gIBK30HQq"/>
  - **Group**: a set of spaces that share content with each other. Each group has a pseudo-user. <roam uid="cqn2EyIWs"/>
  - **`everyone`**: the pseudo-user that public content is shared with. Every caller counts as `everyone`, logged in or not. <roam uid="u2sj1P4VN"/>
  - **Agent**: an AI agent that logs in with a restricted session of its principal (a person or a space), usually read-only. It is not a separate user: it reads what its principal reads. <roam uid="Z4tFuDPOk"/>
- Current state <roam uid="wV0qa8Lj7"/>
  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS" hiddenChildren="2"/>
  - The plugins always act as the space. The Website login (`auth/token` route) also hands over the space session, so spaces, not people, create and administer groups. <roam uid="22z7vxaew"/>
  - `my_user_accounts()` is one level deep: the caller plus the groups the caller belongs to. <roam uid="E5xoEdRTK" hiddenChildren="1"/>
  - A Roam user uid is the same in every graph, and `PlatformAccount` is unique on `(account_local_id, platform)`, so one Roam user is one row, shared by every space they appear in. An Obsidian account is local to its vault: the plugin makes its id from the vault name and a random suffix, but a vault synced between devices or people shares it. <roam uid="0hZ8_lin2"/>
- Ground rules (settled) <roam uid="1Jt5g8iXN"/>
  - Cross-space search must work inside the platforms, not only on the Website. <roam uid="0vB3AfOoR" refs="1"/>
  - `Website` will be added to the `Platform` enum. <roam uid="EZt61u4zE"/>
  - Accounts with passwords stay available. OAuth is an option for cheap re-login, not a requirement. <roam uid="7dKq3Yhma"/>
  - Roam users must not be forced to create a Discourse Graphs account to keep using the plugin. <roam uid="0_gumN62h" hiddenChildren="1"/>
  - A Roam graph token held by our server is not planned for other reasons. It stays open as a security option. <roam uid="TSkb7P3am"/>
  - Groups don't contain groups. Access resolution may add one join, but never a recursive query. <roam uid="spmrIYz0n"/>
  - The hole in the `group_membership` insert policy (anyone could join a uid that had no members yet) is closed before any of this work. Done: ENG-2438, merged 2026-11-05. <roam uid="T_bGruFoR"/>
  - No invitation into a space at the database level. Access comes from the two existing mechanisms: an invitation into the platform, or a group created for sharing. <roam uid="67S6n7Vcu"/>
  - A person reaches a space only through a `PlatformAccount` they have claimed. There is no direct edge from a person to a space. <roam uid="I86s3K6ew" refs="1"/>
- Threat model <roam uid="DM3Hq_Pti"/>
  - **Why it matters:** every stage below is judged by what it lets an attacker do. This section says who the attacker is and what they can reach. The attack scripts walk through each attack step by step, with the limits we ship and the steps that close each gap. <roam uid="ms9rJaiXB"/>
  - Who the attacker is: anyone who holds the password of some space, any space, and knows the victim's platform account id. A co-member is one case, not the only one. <roam uid="65VGj766S" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Attacker skill is no barrier <roam uid="odXXlx9PR" hiddenChildren="5"/>
  - The co-member case, as first described <roam uid="6q9kdzcJl" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - Shared values: platform account values (name, identifiers) are shared on purpose, because Roam shares them across graphs. We harden them by tightening who may write them (accept and audit, then self-reported, then proven), never by keeping a copy per space. <roam uid="ETUWZkrNA"/>
  - Attack scripts <roam uid="97tr4Tlhm" heading="1" refs="1" hiddenChildren="12"/>
- The model: how accounts work at every stage <roam uid="TeM4Yh33h"/>
  - **Why it matters:** this is what stays true from v0 on. The stages change how strong a claim can be and how far it reaches, not this model. <roam uid="TKtnQz1tT"/>
  - Weak and strong claims <roam uid="3lJvV3iJ8" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - Claims: how a person gets a space's access <roam uid="4Rqcs56zH" hiddenChildren="5"/>
  - Sessions <roam uid="m8-wsG3SW" refs="1" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Agents: an agent uses a restricted session of its principal, a space or a person, usually read-only. It is not a separate user and adds nothing to access resolution. See the agent read-only access OpenSpec change. <roam uid="Lnh4NyQ8Q" refs="1"/>
  - Access resolution (sketch) <roam uid="B1gZUizm5" refs="1" hiddenChildren="10"/>
- Staging: accounts v0 and the steps after it <roam uid="JR6Iua-UN" refs="1"/>
  - **Why it matters:** the rest of this page describes the long-term design. The first release of personal accounts will be much smaller: almost certainly no strong proof of identity, and probably nothing that depends on Roam's own login. This section says what that release contains, which steps can follow, and what each step buys in security or in features, so the group can choose the order. <roam uid="lgmo2y52_"/>
  - "Accounts v0" means the first release of personal accounts. It is not the product v0, which is done. <roam uid="CgOzg_SeR"/>
  - Proposed accounts v0 <roam uid="3FQj5hAwM" refs="1" hiddenChildren="9"/>
  - Settled: in v0, a weak claim reaches only the space where it was made <roam uid="AaDDCOTLf" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - What v0 buys <roam uid="ImZ_ulXoW" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - What v0 still allows <roam uid="1uoRV10Su" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - Steps after v0 <roam uid="XepmupGog" hiddenChildren="23"/>
- Decisions index <roam uid="-jcA1NkxH"/>
  - **Why it matters:** one line per decision, with its status and where its details are. When an OpenSpec change settles a decision, its line here links to the change. <roam uid="38YqfRzKN"/>
  - Settled <roam uid="IjElxowcs" hiddenChildren="8"/>
  - Leaning <roam uid="fCwETk8Ye" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Open, needed for v0 <roam uid="49EMX1b_j" hiddenChildren="1"/>
  - Deferred <roam uid="gEZtx7qU2" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Open, after v0 <roam uid="BWtjvQDEN" hiddenChildren="5"/>
- Decision details <roam uid="GU3AW69rv"/>
  - **Why it matters:** each decision in the index above links here, to its options, costs and reasoning. Settled decisions keep their options on record, for the later stages that may revisit them. <roam uid="Ju1YfWQqL"/>
  - How a [personal account](((gav2kohTZ))) is linked to a platform identity: proof layers and packages (open, after v0) <roam uid="HrW3SuczV" refs="1" hiddenChildren="7"/>
  - How far a claim reaches. Settled for v0: a weak claim reaches only the space where it was made (option 2). Later: a strong claim reaches all the platform account's spaces <roam uid="5XbPKQsOm" refs="1" hiddenChildren="2"/>
  - Whether to hide user ids from other clients (leaning: option A) <roam uid="s86_P-XTI" refs="3" hiddenChildren="5"/>
  - Space admin (open, after v0) <roam uid="3l40D2TI3" refs="1" hiddenChildren="7"/>
  - Personal session storage in the plugins (deferred) <roam uid="v-wdJK626" refs="1" hiddenChildren="2"/>
  - Consent for cross-space search (settled for v0: read access is enough) <roam uid="fi-J8nr1F" refs="1" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Personal information before consent (ENG-918) (leaning: names shown, emails hidden; old Roam emails deferred until after v0) <roam uid="sPWWnb1Zg" refs="1" hiddenChildren="5"/>
  - Profile visibility (open, after v0) <roam uid="S4MegNHAq" refs="1" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Which accounts a caller can see (deferred until after v0) <roam uid="aY4D_LNku" refs="1" hiddenChildren="3"/>
- UX touchpoints: where a person must see how they are logged in <roam uid="0m3bnPqzF"/>
  - **Why it matters:** a plugin holds a space session and maybe a personal session, and a claim can be weak, strong, or held by a conflict. The same action gives different results in each state, often silently: RLS returns an empty list, not an error. Every surface below has to tell the person which state applies, or they will read "no access" as "nothing there". Each touchpoint is UI work, so this list is also a cost. <roam uid="Xt_tFK4O3"/>
  - States the UI has to distinguish <roam uid="yLQbi5f0O" hiddenChildren="8"/>
  - Plugins (Roam and Obsidian) <roam uid="OAX4TOvkq" hiddenChildren="13"/>
  - Website <roam uid="iIll2saun" hiddenChildren="5"/>
  - Outside the apps <roam uid="75G9IK3Ox" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Edge cases that change what a touchpoint shows <roam uid="d5N1Dq8K8" hiddenChildren="3"/>
  - Which touchpoints the first release needs: mostly answered by the proposed accounts v0 (((3FQj5hAwM))), which has the Website banner and account page, and in the plugins a status indicator, a connect button and cross-space search. Its wireframes are there too. <roam uid="ibhjghgwf"/>
- Facts to verify before relying on them <roam uid="8okk-_Uer"/>
  - Open <roam uid="-2NuavzaP" hiddenChildren="6"/>
  - Answered <roam uid="mBby9VHAA" hiddenChildren="3"/>
- Appendix: diagrams <roam uid="6ePzuuE00"/>
  - To check: the canvas may still show agents as principals. A redrawn identities diagram, without agent principals, is ready to upload; it probably replaces the first image below. <roam uid="N6qlrPMB6"/>
  - ![](https://firebasestorage.googleapis.com/v0/b/firescript-577a2.appspot.com/o/imgs%2Fapp%2Fdiscourse-graphs%2FoMbD_1Xs-h.svg?alt=media&token=ff8aabdb-be87-480d-932b-ead0847ffe4d) <roam uid="0mR6YMCry"/>
  - {{dg-canvas: [[Canvas/ DG account]]}} <roam uid="fHh1eG1Sn"/>

- [[>]] [[!NOTE]] Project design document: the vision, threat model, stages and decisions for personal accounts <roam uid="S4dKzvDG9"/>
  - This page describes where personal accounts are heading, what can go wrong, the stages we plan to ship, and the decisions that span those stages. Each decision is marked Settled, Leaning, Open or Deferred; the "Decisions index" lists them all. Part of [[Project/Discourse Graph Accounts]]. <roam uid="WOKj5fQ9w"/>
  - How it relates to OpenSpec: accounts v0 becomes one OpenSpec change once its decisions settle, and each later step becomes its own change when it is scheduled. A change's design records a decision in full; this page then marks the decision settled, with a link to the change. <roam uid="gZPUzWdTF" refs="1"/>
- Goal <roam uid="Czog3Tth-"/>
  - A person gets one Discourse Graphs account (a row in `auth.users`) and links to it the platform accounts (`PlatformAccount`) they use in many spaces. <roam uid="c9N0WS5t9"/>
  - That account gives the person every access their spaces have, including access through the groups those spaces belong to. <roam uid="CKv64nUN3"/>
  - The person can link external identities (Google, ORCID, GitHub, ATProto) for login and for visible attribution on published nodes. <roam uid="QJQPmZBiP"/>
  - The person controls how much personal information each audience sees: the public, each group, peers in shared spaces. <roam uid="vzf6T7khx"/>
  - Account management lives on the Website. Accounts are usually created from a platform, but creating one on the Website is also possible. <roam uid="21Ug7tPlh"/>
  - A visitor who reads published content on the Website has an easy path to an account, so they can propose a connected node. <roam uid="qw2XRjp6E"/>
- What personal accounts unblock <roam uid="xf04Pfzph"/>
  - Cross-space search across every space the person can read, without an ad-hoc group. <roam uid="h-4gnZEFx"/>
  - Access through the groups of the person's spaces. <roam uid="VUcgEAHwK"/>
  - Login on the Website without going through a platform. <roam uid="K5GaPtL-U"/>
  - People, not spaces, as group admins. This is where a server-side admin guard (deferred in ENG-1834) belongs. <roam uid="ZaIztzKBk"/>
  - Agents acting for a person: an agent session of a person reads what that person can read. <roam uid="ZMQawpPb-"/>
  - Visible attribution on published nodes, including ORCID or `did:plc` in the JSON-LD export (`prov:wasAttributedTo`). <roam uid="KFl8nD8ZJ"/>
  - One author identity across Roam, Obsidian and the Website. <roam uid="1_RnxGUvX"/>
  - Website-native contribution: a personal space on the `Website` platform holds proposed nodes, which connect to published nodes through cross-space relations (ENG-2334 to ENG-2340). <roam uid="mkRPW2jG7"/>
  - Sharing by a person rather than by a space (the open reciprocal-sharing question on the project page). <roam uid="fSlDNn-H-"/>
- Glossary <roam uid="8wg9mn-Kt"/>
  - **Space**: one Roam graph or Obsidian vault connected to Discourse Graphs. <roam uid="V3WnEIow4"/>
  - **Pseudo-user**: a login (a row in `auth.users`) that stands for something other than a person: a space, a group, or `everyone`. <roam uid="pvL47ThL3"/>
  - **Space password, space session**: the shared credential stored in the platform settings. Every member of the graph can read it. Logging in with it means acting as the space, not as a person. <roam uid="aCzLIN3E9"/>
  - **Personal account, personal session**: a Discourse Graphs account for one person, and a login as that person. Neither exists yet. <roam uid="gav2kohTZ" refs="1"/>
  - **Platform account** (`PlatformAccount`): a person as a platform knows them. A Roam user has the same uid, so the same platform account, in every graph. An Obsidian platform account belongs to one vault. <roam uid="QH3QWTy6q"/>
  - **`LocalAccess`**: the record that a platform account takes part in a space. <roam uid="u7kJsZCjS"/>
  - **Co-member**: someone in the same space, who therefore holds the space password and can act as the space. **Space password holder**: anyone who holds the password of some space, any space. The threat model uses this wider term, because many attacks don't need the attacker to share a space with the victim. <roam uid="PrKq7VlbT"/>
  - **Claim**: a personal account's statement "this platform account is me". It is stored on the platform account (`dg_account`). <roam uid="_ditzi8bq"/>
  - **Vouching space**: the space whose session made the claim. Because that session is shared, it shows only that someone in that space made the claim, not who. <roam uid="w9yVmbPyd"/>
  - **Attestation level**: how well a claim is proven, as stored on the claim. `asserted` is a weak claim; the other levels are kinds of strong claim, or a held one. <roam uid="0ifLRtPpZ" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - **Weak claim, strong claim**: a weak claim's only evidence is the space session that made it, so any holder of that space's password could have made it; in v0 it reaches only that space. A strong claim carries a proof a password holder can't fake, and can reach all the platform account's spaces and carry attribution. Older sections call these an access claim and an identity claim. The difference is the attestation level, not a different record. <roam uid="xwIIr5Cdw"/>
  - **Reach**: the spaces a person can act for through their claims. <roam uid="_blIoPRFG"/>
  - **Lease**: a limit on how long a person's access through a space lasts after they stop using the plugin there (`LocalAccess.last_seen`). Leaning: unlimited, so no expiry in v0. <roam uid="gegO9HCwc"/>
  - **Cap**: a limit on what a claim or a grant allows, for example read-only. <roam uid="gIBK30HQq"/>
  - **Group**: a set of spaces that share content with each other. Each group has a pseudo-user. <roam uid="cqn2EyIWs"/>
  - **`everyone`**: the pseudo-user that public content is shared with. Every caller counts as `everyone`, logged in or not. <roam uid="u2sj1P4VN"/>
  - **Agent**: an AI agent that logs in with a restricted session of its principal (a person or a space), usually read-only. It is not a separate user: it reads what its principal reads. <roam uid="Z4tFuDPOk"/>

  - Today `auth.users` holds only non-person principals. <roam uid="v4T3sJ7nT" hiddenChildren="4"/>
  - A person exists only as a `PlatformAccount` row inside spaces, with `dg_account` empty. <roam uid="IYCyffXJS" hiddenChildren="2"/>

The refactor is done, and I read the whole page back to confirm the new order. The [spec page](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/H3a0tja8D) now goes:
- **Note:** rewritten to say this is the project design document, and how it relates to OpenSpec.
- **Goal** and **What personal accounts unblock**, unchanged except for removing the empty separator.
- **Glossary:** weak and strong claims are now the main terms. "Space password holder" is added. The attestation levels are corrected. Leases lean towards unlimited.
- **Current state** and **Ground rules (settled):** the Obsidian answer is folded in, and the `group_membership` hole is marked done (ENG-2438).
- **[Threat model](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/DM3Hq_Pti) (new):** who the attacker is, why skill is no barrier, the rule for shared values, the original co-member text (corrected), and the attack scripts.
- **[The model](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/TeM4Yh33h) (new):** weak and strong claims, the claim model, sessions (delivery now settled, social login through the Website), agents, and access resolution. The claim-writes question in access resolution is marked settled by ENG-2447.
- **Staging:** adds the search-consent cost. The conflicting-claims question now mentions the shared row. The security lines for the email match and agreement between spaces are corrected.
- **[Decisions index](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/-jcA1NkxH) (new):** each line links to its details with a `((ref))`.
- **[Decision details](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/GU3AW69rv) (new):** the long sections, each heading marked with its status.
- **UX touchpoints:** state names updated, and the first-release question points to the v0 proposal.
- **Facts to verify:** split into Open and Answered, with social login added as answered.
- **[Appendix: diagrams](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/6ePzuuE00)** holds the image and the canvas.

Every existing block was moved, not copied, so references to it still work. I deleted only three blocks: the separator, and the two parents left empty ("WIP on attack vectors" and "Other open decisions").

**Still to do:**
- **Old wording in the details:** the decision details still use L-numbers and `asserted` / `attested` in places. Only the headings and wrong claims were updated.
- **Diagrams:** the redrawn identities SVG isn't uploaded, and the canvas may still show agents.
- **A changed reference:** one block I rewrote (the OpenSpec line in the note) is referenced from somewhere else, which will now show the new text.

content.text: Both restructurings are done. Next, the old vocabulary. I'm searching the page for the blocks that still use it (a read).

[
  [
    "U_5nSbh0a",
    "The token shows that the submitter is an admin. It doesn't say which Roam user they are. The flag should only land on a `PlatformAccount` whose claim is stronger than `asserted`, or the same token should attest the submitter first."
  ],
  [
    "T-Fu8N8v5",
    "The question for each stage is how far a weak claim reaches, and what a co-member gains by forging one."
  ],
  [
    "sXHPyZ9TX",
    "Own attribution: if attribution export requires `attested`, the person sees that their published nodes carry no `prov:wasAttributedTo`, and how to raise the claim level."
  ],
  [
    "LT9VSLIoK",
    "`attested`: proven by a check that a space password holder can't fake, such as a Roam backend token (L6) or a Roam sign-in token (L8). Email binding (L1) counts only once the email record itself can't be written under a space login (see the threat model, attack 2)."
  ],
  [
    "NPNnmg2d7",
    "A co-member sees the victim's Roam uid in the graph, since the plugin reads every member's uid to fill in `PlatformAccount`. A member of a space that shares a group with one of the victim's spaces can read it from `PlatformAccount` or `my_accounts`."
  ],
  [
    "w7SPEavvQ",
    "Example policy: export `prov:wasAttributedTo` only for `attested` links."
  ],
  [
    "YyVfTf1I1",
    "**Why it matters:** every admin power is something any holder of the space password can do today, for example rotating that password or joining groups for the space. The weaker the admin proof, the easier it is for a co-member to take those powers, so the proof and the list of powers have to be decided together."
  ],
  [
    "xp07QYFwB",
    "L5: Admin approval. The space admin confirms identity claims in that space. Set aside: having admins approve someone's identity feels wrong in general."
  ],
  [
    "qbzJP8qlz",
    "An access claim is an `asserted` claim: \"I am this platform account\", vouched for only by one space's session. If it gives access only in that space, a forger gains nothing they don't already have."
  ],
  [
    "28rjLezNq",
    "An `asserted` claim gives access only in the vouching space."
  ],
  [
    "eNir7ER3F",
    "Stops a co-member who only uses the plugin. It doesn't stop one who sends a hand-made request with the space password, because nothing but the victim's own client can see the victim's email."
  ],
  [
    "yhMBFbag9",
    "Forgeable on every platform: the plugin sends the report under the space session, so a co-member who holds the space password can report themselves as admin. L8 would prove which Roam user is calling, but not that this user is an admin. In Roam, L6 closes the gap for the admin who supplies a backend token: only admins can create one, and the same token lets our server attest which Roam user they are. That admin moves to the proven tier; other admins stay guessed."
  ],
  [
    "AM08ShSzs",
    "The binding would come from the plugin, as it does in Roam. But an Obsidian vault rarely has co-members who could forge it, so L1 adds less there."
  ],
  [
    "65VGj766S",
    "Who the attacker is: anyone who holds the password of some space, any space, and knows the victim's platform account id. A co-member is one case, not the only one."
  ],
  [
    "KS_8ViwDE",
    "Every claim is an identity claim. Access covers every space where the `PlatformAccount` has `LocalAccess`."
  ],
  [
    "F5NMd6BX2",
    "`corroborated`: two or more spaces recorded the same platform account details before the claim (layer L2). As specified, this is not a proof: one person can control two spaces (see the threat model, attack 3)."
  ],
  [
    "jPAJgfeYD",
    "1. Mallory gets a space login: lab-graph's, if she is a co-member, or her own graph M's. **[checked]**"
  ],
  [
    "Qr1nAWi-I",
    "The weak point is the source of the uid-to-email binding. Only the user's own client can read their email, and it reports it under the shared space session. A co-member who calls our API with the space password can report any email for any uid, and no other member's plugin can confirm or contradict it. Stored `AgentIdentifier` rows can also be poisoned, because RLS lets space editors write identifiers of unclaimed accounts."
  ],
  [
    "77QWvUHKp",
    "**The victim's Roam account id.** A co-member sees it in the graph: the plugin reads every member's account id to fill in the `PlatformAccount` rows **[checked]** (confirmed by the user). A member of a space that shares a group with one of the victim's spaces can read the victim's `PlatformAccount` row, id and name included **[checked]** (`platform_account_select_policy` through `accounts_in_my_partial_spaces`, `account.sql`)."
  ],

content.text:
All of it is done, and I read the changed sections back.

**What you asked for**
- **"What personal accounts unblock"** is now split in two:
  - **With accounts v0:** search across connected spaces, access through those spaces' groups, Website login, and people as group admins.
  - **After v0:** agents acting for a person, attribution, one author identity, contributing from the Website, and sharing by a person. I added a line to the search item saying strong claims widen it later.
- **"Steps after v0"** keeps deletion first and then has three groups, not two:
  - [Claim hardening](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/K58clDqAt): notify, email match, several emails, agreement between spaces, device keys, and the two Roam proofs.
  - [Other security](https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/phtI-XMrs): space admins, retiring the space login, and session management. These protect the space or the account rather than the claim, and fit neither of your groups. If you'd rather have only two groups, say where they should go.

content.text:
The wording is misleading. The login itself already happens on the Website, through Supabase's OAuth server; nobody proposes doing OAuth inside the plugin.

What the question was really asking is the last step: **how the plugin gets its session back** once the person has logged in on the Website. There are two ways:
- **Redirect back to the plugin.** In Roam, a popup on the Website posts the authorization code back to the Roam page. In Obsidian, an `obsidian://` handler receives it. The plugin then exchanges the code for its own tokens. This is the standard OAuth ending.
- **Polling.** The Website receives the result, and the plugin collects it with the one-time `secret_token`. This always works, because the plugin never has to receive the redirect.

The spec already says the first is nice to have and the second is the fallback (HmGIe3SsJ). So the open fact is only whether the first works in each plugin.

I'd reword the entry to: "After the Website login, can the plugin receive the result directly (a popup posting back to the Roam page; an `obsidian://` handler), or does it always collect it with the `secret_token` fallback?" Or, if you're happy to always use the fallback, I'd move the entry to Answered. Which would you prefer?

message.content: Hmmm... I suspect the first, but let's write it in terms of mhat's the difference from the user point of view? When you start from the platform, the platform account is known; if there is a user behind it, we may need to login on the web to set the web cookies, and then tell the platform that is done, but before that, do we accept to act as the user within the platform? My basic intuition is that there is little the user can do _on the platform_ that is not allowed simply by virtue of being logged into the platform with the platform account. (Account management happens on the web and requires login, of course.) Let's think of it with a concrete example: If I have connected many spaces through my user account, I think I should be able to do a cross-space search on the platform by virtue of being logged into the platform. Or is that a security risk I'm missing?

content.text:
Yes, that would be a real risk. Your intuition holds inside the current space, but cross-space search is exactly where it breaks.

**Why: our server never sees the Roam login.** Roam knows Alice is logged in, but the plugin talks to our server under lab-graph's shared space login. All the server learns is that the request comes from someone with lab-graph's password. If the plugin also says "I'm Roam user Alice", the server can only take its word. So acting as the user "by virtue of being logged into the platform" means trusting the uid the plugin reports.

Concretely, assuming Alice has connected lab-graph and team-graph, and Mallory is in lab-graph only:
1. Mallory reads lab-graph's space password from the graph's settings page. (Checked in code.)
2. She sends a search request by hand under lab-graph's login, saying "I'm Alice's uid". (Her plugin would send her own uid, so she bypasses it.)
3. If the server serves the person behind that uid, the search covers team-graph, where Mallory has no access.

Alice's claim can be perfectly genuine and this still works. The claim answers "is this platform account Alice?" The attack exploits a different question: "is this request from Alice?" Under a shared space login, nothing answers that second question. The personal session from the Website login is what answers it. That's why the narrow-reach decision alone doesn't cover this case.

**What you can already do without a personal session.** Anything the space can do, in that space. So for everything within the current graph, you're right that a web login adds nothing. It matters only for reaching beyond the space (cross-space search) and for acting as the person (group admin and similar).

**Two later steps would make your intuition work**, because each proves who is sending a request:
- **Device keys.** A request signed by Alice's registered device key shows it comes from her device. The plugin could then act as her for cross-space search without a Website session. The same caveat as for session storage applies: other Roam extensions can use the key while the page is open.
- **Proof from Roam's login** (the Firebase token). It proves the request is from Roam user Alice. It's blocked by Roam's terms.

**From the user's point of view, both handback options feel the same.** Alice clicks Connect, a Website popup or tab opens, and she logs in. If the Website cookie is still valid, she only confirms. Then the plugin is connected. With a direct handback, the popup closes itself. With polling, she's left with a tab that says "you can close this". Either way it's once per device, and whether she has to do it again after a reload depends on the deferred session-storage decision.

I'd reword the facts entry as: "After the Website login, can the plugin receive the result directly (a popup posting back to Roam; an `obsidian://` handler), so the Website tab closes itself? Otherwise the plugin collects it with `secret_token`. For the person, the difference is only whether a tab is left open." I'd also add to the Sessions block why a personal session is needed even though the person is already logged into the platform, with the attack above. Should I do both?

content.text:
Content first, then the format.

**A proposed narrative.** It runs about 14 slides, built for people who heard the earlier version:

1. **Title.**
2. **What changed since you last heard this.** We split the work into stages, and v0 is small. Agents became restricted sessions, not accounts. The attacker turned out to be wider than a co-member. The spec page is now a project design document.
3. **Why personal accounts.** One person, many spaces. Today everything acts as the space.
4. **Today, in one picture:** the identities diagram, solid lines only.
5. **The core problem.** A space password is shared, and our server never sees the platform's login. So anyone holding a space password can say "I'm Alice" and we can't tell.
6. **Weak and strong claims:** one definition, used throughout the rest of the deck.
7. **Accounts v0.** Connect from the plugin, log in on the Website, and come back connected. The plugin keeps two sessions. The v0 account-page wireframe goes here.
8. **What v0 buys, and what it costs.** It buys search across connected spaces, Website login, and people as group admins. It costs one connection per space, and security stays the same as today.
9. **Attack 1, step by step:** a forged claim, made harmless by the narrow reach.
10. **Risks we accept in v0.** A forged claim shows on the forger's account page. Conflicting claims are still open. Every password holder acts as the space until there are admins (attack 4).
11. **After v0, the ladder.** Deletion comes first, then three columns: claim hardening, other security, and expanded use cases.
12. **Why hardening is harder than it looks.** Attacks 2 and 3 (a faked email match, forged agreement between spaces) lead to device keys and Roam's server as the real proofs.
13. **Attacker skill is no barrier:** the LLM argument, on one slide.
14. **Decisions.** What's settled, what's still open for v0 (conflicting claims), what's deferred, and what we need from the team.
15. **Order of work:** MCP token handoff, then agent read-only access, then accounts v0.

**Questions that change the content:**
1. **When:** do you want dates, or just the order of work? I don't know the schedule beyond that order.
2. **Time slot:** with 15–20 minutes I'd fold 12 and 13 into one slide and leave the attacks after attack 1 for questions.
3. **Asks:** what do you want the team to decide or weigh in on? Conflicting claims is the obvious one. Michael's note on forcing accounts could be another.
4. **The shared-account issue candidate:** include it as "found along the way", or leave it out?

**Format: reveal.js with SVG is easier for me than PowerPoint, and I don't need a skill for it.**
- A deck is one HTML file with reveal.js pinned from a CDN, and I hand you the file.
- SVG diagrams go inline, so each one is part of the slide, not a separate image.
- **Step-by-step attacks come for free:** reveal.js fragments work on SVG groups, so each arrow or label appears on the next keypress. That's the "slides showing the steps" you asked for at the start.
- The same file can later be embedded in Roam through the iframe wrapper, as we planned for the attack slides.
- The figures I've already made (the identities diagram and the wireframes) can go in as they are.

PowerPoint would need the pptx skill, and step-by-step builds are clumsier there.

content.text:
Pandoc is just as easy for me, and better for you, since you can edit the text directly. You have pandoc 3.14 installed, which handles everything below.

- **Text slides:** plain markdown. `#` starts a slide, `::: notes` holds speaker notes, `::: incremental` reveals bullets one by one, and `{.fragment}` reveals any single element.
- **Figures:** each SVG stays its own file, referenced as `![](figure.svg)`. So the markdown stays readable, and I can render and check each figure on its own.
- **Step-by-step attacks:** I draw one SVG per step on the same fixed layout, then stack them with reveal.js's `r-stack`:
  ```
  ::: {.r-stack}
  ![](attack1-step1.svg)
  ![](attack1-step2.svg){.fragment}
  ![](attack1-step3.svg){.fragment}
  :::
  ```
  Each keypress lays the next step over the previous one in the same place, which gives the effect of arrows appearing. It's simpler than fragments inside one inline SVG, and it keeps raw HTML out of the markdown.
- **Build:** `pandoc -t revealjs -s --embed-resources deck.md -o deck.html` gives one self-contained HTML file. That suits the Roam iframe wrapper later, and works offline in the meeting. I'd put a one-line build script next to the deck in `dg_agent_diagrams/`.

If you have a reveal.js theme or pandoc template you normally use, point me to it and I'll build with it. Otherwise I'll use the default white theme.

Back to content: the four questions from my last message still decide what goes in. They were the dates or order of work, the time slot, what you want the team to decide, and whether to include the shared-account issue candidate.
